title: Residual-Guided Global-Drive Design in Trapped-Ion Quantum Simulators
abstract: Trapped-ion quantum simulators are powerful platforms for exploring many-body physics, yet engineering of arbitrary interaction graphs remains a central challenge. To leverage the intrinsic structure of native motional modes and thereby enhance programmability, a residual-guided optimization protocol is introduced for the systematic design of multi-tone global drive spectra. While the achievable interaction fidelity is fundamentally bounded by the available motional modes, this adaptive strategy converges on the theoretical limit using a number of laser tones that scales nearly linearly with system size. The versatility of this method enables the synthesis of both long-range and traditionally difficult short-range coupling topologies. Additionally, by incorporating a penalty for residual motional excitation, the algorithm effectively mitigates errors associated with incomplete closure of phase-space trajectories. Overall, this scalable framework significantly expands the programmable capabilities of trapped-ion architectures while maintaining low computational overhead and high potential for experimental implementation.
summary: This paper presents Residual-Guided Drive Design (RGDD), a novel optimization protocol for engineering arbitrary interaction graphs in trapped-ion quantum simulators. RGDD iteratively adds laser tones to synthesize a target Hamiltonian while minimizing infidelity and controlling motional excitation errors. This scalable framework significantly expands the programmable capabilities of trapped-ion quantum computing platforms.
main_problem: The central challenge is designing a compact set of global drive spectra to synthesize a target interaction Hamiltonian in trapped-ion quantum simulators with high fidelity.
main_result: The Residual-Guided Drive Design (RGDD) protocol systematically achieves near-theoretical fidelity bounds using a number of laser tones that scales nearly linearly with system size.
method: RGDD is an incremental optimization strategy that iteratively adds global laser tones, guided by the residual error, to minimize the cosine infidelity between the synthesized and target interaction.
model_or_system: The system is trapped-ion quantum simulators, where interactions are modeled using long-range Ising-type Hamiltonians generated by multi-tone global drive laser fields.
key_observables: Cosine infidelity ($I$), minimum number of tones ($M_{min}$), and residual motional excitation ($\alpha_k$).
important_parameters: Gate time ($t_g$), penalty coefficient ($\lambda_a$), and the ratio of gate time to baseline time ($s = t_g/t_{g0}$).
main_assumptions: The accessible interaction space is fundamentally constrained by the native motional modes of the ion crystal.
figures_summary: Figures compare tone-count scaling (RGDD vs. NNLS) and closure error across different power-law targets; Figure 6 compares infidelity vs. tone count for RGDD versus equal-spacing placement.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the RGDD protocol, details the optimization objective incorporating a closure penalty, and then analyzes its performance by comparing it against baseline methods (like NNLS) and by investigating the trade-off between infidelity and closure error as a function of gate time.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the engineering challenge of controlling complex many-body interactions in trapped ions, providing a scalable, systematic method for designing the required laser fields.

The selected tones are then used to synthesize the target Hamiltonian, with their µm and Ωm optimized toward the lowest infidelity achievable at the current step.
